display: Youth football coach (U13–U15) at a club academy in São Paulo, CBF B-licence, six years with the same club. I build technical midfielders and teams that play out from the back. The academy breaks from mid-December to late February.

signals.text: I'm looking for a paid coaching job abroad during the mid-December to late-February break: a camp, a clinic, a short stint at an academy, anything.
I need a position that comes with a stipend, or a place where my family can visit or have their travel covered.
My club contract forbids any outside coaching between March and early December, so only a window that starts in mid-December works for me.
The off-season income matters a lot this year. Without it I can't cover even the usual family trip.
I have a good Argentine coaching friend who runs a clinic in Rosario in January, and I couldn't afford the flight. Anything with a stipend at that kind of event would let me go.
My U14 team is second in the regional group with five games left, and my left side has no one who can overlap. I need a left-back or a way to fix that.
I'm testing a 7v7 with five zones I saw in a Spanish academy video, and I'm looking for more sessions like it from other academies.
I'm getting ready for a possible tryout or coaching interview in English. I'm practising short phrases and want honest feedback from native speakers.
I'd like to turn my notebooks (about 400 sessions) into something shareable, but I haven't found the time or the format.
I'm redoing a family kitchen with my brother-in-law, so my weekends are taken up with demolition and plumbing for now.
I coach my daughter's under-10 girls futsal team on Saturdays and I'm looking for fun, simple drills for nine-year-olds, some of whom mostly want to talk.
I'm tired. I'm juggling the club, family health logistics and a house project, and I have little time for myself.

offers.text: I can run youth football sessions (U12–U16) in English or Spanish, with a clear plan for each session.
I can run a clinic or camp on building play from the back, pressing triggers and small-sided games.
I have about 400 written training sessions sorted by theme, and I can adapt them to a club's level and age group.
I do video analysis with an action camera and Hudl. After each match I cut clips for the players to review.
I have a track record of developing technically clean midfielders. Two former players are now in professional academies.
I'm CBF B-licence certified and have worked six years at the same academy.
I can trade ideas with Spanish-speaking coaches, including Argentine ones, on training methods and session design.
I'm available for work abroad from mid-December to late February.
I can talk through how I'd explain football to parents, who often trust my work with their sons' technical development.

catchers.hypo: We're an academy in Spain/Portugal/Argentina/the US and we need an extra coach for our winter camp from late December to February. We can offer a stipend and accommodation. Do you know anyone?
catchers.can: I'm available in that window and can run sessions in English or Spanish. I'd need the stipend to cover some travel for my family.
catchers.confirm: Does the camp run inside mid-December to late February and offer a stipend or travel support?

catchers.hypo: I organise a winter football clinic in January and want a coach who can teach build-up from the back to 12–15 year olds. Can you present a session?
catchers.can: I can design and lead a build-up and pressing-trigger session based on my notebooks, and cut video clips for the players afterwards.
catchers.confirm: Is the clinic for players aged 12–15 and willing to cover at least some of the coach's travel?

catchers.hypo: I'm a young coach starting with a U13 team and I'm lost with session planning. Can someone look at my plans?
catchers.can: I can review plans, share how I structure a session, and suggest drills from my notebooks.
catchers.confirm: Is this a youth team (U10–U16) where session planning is the main difficulty, rather than first-team tactics?

catchers.hypo: I run a coaching education programme and want practising coaches to share real session plans. Would you contribute?
catchers.can: I can share a curated set of my sessions, sorted by theme, in English or Portuguese.
catchers.confirm: Is the programme for youth coaches and does it respect the author's credit for shared plans?

catchers.hypo: My family member needs dialysis and I'm trying to understand the costs, transport and what insurance covers in São Paulo. Has anyone been through this?
catchers.can: I can share what I've learned from taking my own family member to sessions three times a week, and my sister Ana, who helps with costs, could add her view.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking for practical experience with dialysis logistics and costs in São Paulo, rather than medical advice?

catchers.hypo: I run a dental clinic in São Paulo and need a reliable assistant who is patient and organised. Do you know anyone?
catchers.can: My wife Camila is a dental assistant. I can pass the message to her.
catchers.confirm: Is the role for a dental assistant in São Paulo, and is the clinic open to hearing from someone currently employed elsewhere?

catchers.hypo: My club in Campinas is looking for a youth coach or a consultant for our U13 group. Can you recommend someone?
catchers.can: I can recommend myself for a consultancy or workshop, and my sister Ana lives in Campinas, so a visit is easy to arrange. Any in-season work needs my club's permission.
catchers.confirm: Is this a one-off workshop or an off-season role, rather than a position that overlaps with March to early December?

catchers.hypo: We have a girl who loves football and doesn't have a team near São Paulo. Do you know of a team for under-10s?
catchers.can: I coach an under-10 girls futsal team on Saturday mornings and can share how we welcome new players.
catchers.confirm: Is the player around 8–10 years old and looking for a casual futsal team in São Paulo?

catchers.hypo: I have a left-back around 13 or 14 who can overlap and is looking for a club in São Paulo. Would you take a look?
catchers.can: I can watch him in a training session and give honest feedback, though any transfer is up to my club.
catchers.confirm: Is the player a left-back aged 13–14 in the São Paulo area, with the family aware that it's only a look and not a promise of a place?

forbids.text: I can't do any outside coaching work between March and early December. My contract forbids it.
I can only travel for work between mid-December and late February.
I won't take a job abroad that gives my family no way to visit and no stipend that covers their travel.
I don't share my family's financial details or bank information.
I won't poach players or contact players behind the back of the club.

projects.name: Off-season coaching stint abroad
projects.text: Looking for a camp, clinic or short academy role abroad during the December–February break, with a stipend or family travel support.

projects.name: Training notebook library
projects.text: Turning about 400 handwritten sessions into a structured, shareable collection for youth coaches.

policy.t1: When there's a real opportunity, I'll share my contract limits, my December–February availability and that I'm interested in coaching abroad during the break, including the need for a stipend or family travel support.
policy.t2: Once the other side is clear and the fit is strong, I'll explain why off-season income matters, including that a family member's medical costs are growing.
policy.never: Family bank details and my private doubts about my career.
